summary: Intermittent serving degradation from tenant burst exposing autoscale sizing gap
description:
Issue summary:
Customer CloudPaper AI reports repeated timeouts (client 504) and elevated p95/p99 token latency for requests pinned to their dedicated GPU reservation between 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC and ongoing. Impact is intermittent but recurring during tenant-driven bursts.

Impact:
- Multiple production requests timing out (504) and streaming disconnects reported by the customer.
- Elevated p95 (2.3s -> 7s) and p99 tail spikes up to 18s for short text generation endpoints.
- Customer facing UX regressions and increased error rate; they asked for urgent mitigation.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation: redwood-dedicated-cc-prod-09 (4x A100s), us-east cluster
- Customer traffic pattern: frequent long-sequence streaming jobs and a handful of concurrent long-stream sessions from a single tenant process.
- Autoscale policy: target based on pod GPU utilization (avg), min_replicas=1, max_replicas=6, cooldown=300s.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant issues a sudden burst of 30 concurrent long-seq streaming requests (seq_len ~ 2048).
2) Pods serving the tenant show near-saturation on SM% and kernel queuing increases.
3) Autoscaler does not scale quickly because average GPU util stays under threshold (due to a mix of idle short requests and a few saturated pods).
4) Scheduler queues requests, micro-batches overlap, KV cache thrash observed, leading to p95/p99 spikes and 504s.

Observed behavior:
- GPU SM% per-saturated pod >95% for sustained periods.
- Cluster-level GPU utilization averaged ~62% (below autoscale trigger).
- Request queue depth on the per-tenant routing queue climbed >200 for short windows.
- Streaming sessions aborted after client-side 30s timeout (customer SDK default).

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should react to per-pod saturation or queue length and bring up capacity fast enough to maintain p95 below 2s for this workload pattern.

Artifacts attached / logs referenced:
- Grafana dashboards: serving/runtime/p95, node/gpu-sm, autoscale/activity (links provided to customer and infra).
- Sample traces: trace IDs provided to SRE channel.
- Kernel logs: show repeated SM stalls and occasional nvlink retries.

Initial triage summary:
- Hypothesis: Autoscaler policy relying solely on average GPU utilization masks localized saturation caused by uneven traffic distribution (noisy tenant).
- Secondary contributor: Long-sequence streaming jobs hold GPU context and induce KV cache churn that increases effective per-request cost.
- Immediate mitigation options: temporary tenant isolation (soft reservation), add per-tenant queue-based scaling metric, or increase min_replicas for this reservation.
comments: 2026-03-10 Elena Park (Support): Received report from CloudPaper AI. They included example request IDs and SDK logs showing client 504s. Marking P1 and escalating to SRE because customer is on dedicated reservation.
2026-03-10 Marcus Li (SRE): Acknowledged. Pulling relevant dashboards and queue metrics. Asked customer for exact request IDs and timestamps (provided). Assigned to Marcus Li (SRE) and Triage team.

2026-03-10 Marcus Li (SRE): Observed sustained SM% spikes on two pods pinned to cloudpaper-tenant shard. Cluster-level util is moderate; per-pod distribution is skewed. Uploading screenshots to ticket and #support-us-east channel.

2026-03-11 Support: Notified customer we are investigating and proposed a short-term mitigation: increase min_replicas to 2 for the reservation and enable tenant soft-reservation. Customer approved temporary change.

2026-03-11 Ops (Automation): Applied temporary override: redwood-dedicated-cc-prod-09 min_replicas=2 for CloudPaper AI reservation. Observed immediate reduction in p95 from ~7s to ~2.4s during a smaller repeat burst. Metrics attached.

2026-03-11 Marcus Li (SRE): Performed deeper trace analysis. Found queue depth spikes correlate with long-seq streaming sessions from a small set of client IPs. Autoscaler cooldown of 300s prevented fast scaling during short spikes. Filed follow-up action to change scaling signal to include per-pod 95th percentile GPU latency / request queue length.

2026-03-12 Product (Platform): Proposed autoscaler enhancement RFC to consider per-pod latency and queue backlog as scaling signals. Referenced PR #4802 that adds a queue-based metric collector (staging validation in progress).
2026-03-12 CloudPaper AI (Customer): Confirmed temporary improvement but requested a durable fix. Asked for timeline for autoscale change or a recommended long-term reservation sizing guideline.

2026-03-12 Marcus Li (SRE): Committed to two-track plan: 1) short-term policy change + reservation sizing recommendation within 48 hours, 2) medium-term autoscaler change in ~2-3 sprints with a canary rollout. Added related_confluence link for runbook updates.
investigation_notes: Checked serving-runtime logs for noisy-tenant markers: tenant_id=cloudpaper-42 shows high long-seq session counts at 2026-03-09 22:03-22:18 UTC.
Kernel telemetry: increased SM stalls and higher memory copy times on affected pods; nvlink errors transient but not primary root cause.
Autoscaler analysis: current metric is cluster_avg_gpu_utilization. This allowed saturated pods to be masked by idle or low-util pods in the same reservation.
KV cache observations: repeated cache misses when requests hit newly scaled pods, causing additional token latency for affected sessions.

Reproduction in staging: simulated 25 concurrent long-seq streams; observed same pattern when autoscale uses average util with long cooldowns. Changing scale signal to per-pod 90th percentile GPU latency reduced tail significantly.
Related historical tickets: see SUP-9271 (sustained throughput drop), SUP-48210 (pipeline saturation). Patterns overlap but root cause here is autoscale signal masking localized saturation.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation applied: min_replicas increased to 2 for the customer's reservation and soft-reservation applied to reduce noisy-tenant spillover. Customer reports immediate improvement; p95 back to ~2s in observed windows.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Short term: provide CloudPaper AI sizing guidance (recommend increasing reserved GPUs for sustained long-seq workloads or using smaller per-stream batching) and update runbook. ETA: 48 hours.
- Medium term: implement autoscaler to include per-pod queue-length / p95 latency as a scaling signal and reduce cooldown for surge handling. PR #4802 implementing queue-based metric collector is in review; canary rollout scheduled for next sprint.

Follow-ups:
- Update Dedicated Autoscale Runbook to include noisy-tenant isolation steps.
- Consider per-tenant soft reservations for heavy long-seq workflows.
- Track action item ENG-OPS-1753 to validate autoscaler changes across 2 clusters.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-11: Temporary min_replicas=2 override rolled for customer reservation by ops-automation; watch metrics for 24h.
2026-03-12: Customer confirmed reduction in error rate; remaining action is product change to autoscaler and runbook update.
ENG-OPS-1753 created to track autoscaler enhancement and runbook updates.
